title: Role-Protected Moderation
body_html:
P02 is the central implementation. The required reduced P03 portfolio covers CORS and CSRF. P01 continues as a semester-project transfer.

This meeting has 60 content minutes. The full required work may continue until the actual teacher-set deadline.
task: Individual predictions and your own evidence

title: The extracted workspace
body_html:
Find the extracted package root and the provisioned environment. Record the versions you actually observe.

The prescribed pair is Node 24.21.0 and npm 11.19.0. A mismatch or missing dependency is a blocking condition to record.
task: Use the beginner guide for the exact preflight route

title: Prediction: a claimed role
body_html:
A report belongs to one synthetic fixture user. A request body claims a different owner and an administrator role.

Which supplied component can establish the acting principal? Which component can establish the stored owner?
task: Write the prediction before reading the mechanism

title: Trusted input provenance
body_html: The authentication fixture supplies the principal. The route supplies a constant action. The repository supplies the stored report.
task: Trace the source of role and ownership in the supplied files

title: Roles and ownership
body_html:
ConceptEvidence to inspect
OwnerThe report’s stored ownerId and the principal’s id
MemberThe supplied member permission set
ModeratorThe supplied moderator permission set
AdministratorThe supplied admin permission set

Ownership describes a relationship. Each action uses its own supplied permission rule.
task: Avoid replacing action-specific rules with a role ranking

title: Prediction: four outcomes
body_html:
• An owner requests an allowed action.
  • An unrelated member requests an ordinary protected action.
  • A configured route conceals a forbidden result.
  • A permitted action reaches a report in the wrong state.
task: Predict each outcome and the component that decides it

title: The assessed edit boundary
body_html:
The P02 assessed edit is:

projects/p02/student/src/authorization-policy.js

Supplied support, tests and dependencies remain outside the assessed edit. A boundary check reports allowed paths only.
task: Keep a locator for your own policy change

title: Policy obligations
body_html:
• Handle unsupported actions at middleware construction.
  • Use the trusted principal and stored report.
  • Retain the configured denial and concealment rule.
  • Forward unexpected runtime errors through the supplied error path.
task: Use the project contract while implementing

title: Implementation interval
body_html:
Continue the policy in the permitted file. Keep the supplied fixtures and support files intact.

If the qualified execution lane is unavailable, trace source and retain a truthful draft. Record the precise blocking condition.
task: Five minutes of individual work

title: Named checks and failure classes
body_html:
Baseline, objective and regression results have separate names and records. The starter objective failures need the documented assertion signatures.

A missing command, parser error, timeout, crash or signal is an infrastructure incident.
task: Use the exact check route in the beginner guide

title: Implementation checkpoint
body_html:
The implementation interval ends here. Record what your own policy does and what remains unresolved.

The full P02 estimate exceeds this interval. An incomplete implementation stays visible in the draft.
task: Retain the last trustworthy state before observation

title: Prediction: the meaning of 404
body_html:
You see a public 404 response from a protected report route.

What evidence would distinguish a missing report from a configured concealed refusal?
task: Predict the required locator before the explanation

title: Denial and concealment
body_html: Record the route’s configured disclosure policy alongside the public outcome. Ordinary refusal and concealed refusal need different explanations.
task: Keep configuration and evidence class with the observation

title: Permission and report state
body_html: Return to the state prediction recorded at minutes 10–12. Inspect or observe the permitted action on an invalid state using fresh fixtures.
task: Record stored state before and after the case

title: One load and a bounded snapshot
body_html:
Record how you measured one resource load. Inspect the flat frozen snapshot and the call to the supplied continuation.

A source or callback witness leaves actual Express order and database concurrency unverified.
task: Give the observation a class and a locator

title: One falsifiable Gemini claim
body_html:
Example claim to critique: A 404 response proves that the report is missing.

Prepare one sanitised code or trace excerpt. Remove tokens, cookies, private records and unnecessary personal data.
task: Ask for the claim analysis, without a complete solution

title: The actual exchange
body_html:
Use the real Gemini route described in the guide. Preserve only the relevant actual prompt and response excerpt.

If access is blocked, record the block. A separately authorised alternative needs its own prior teacher policy.
task: Keep model output separate from your own observation

title: The independent verdict
body_html:
VerdictRequired explanation
ACCEPTEDEvidence supports the bounded claim
REJECTEDA located counterexample contradicts it
PARTIALLY ACCEPTEDSpecify the supported scope and correction
UNKNOWNName the evidence still missing
task: Check the claim against your located source, test or observation

title: Evidence class and inference
body_html:
Recorded witnessClass and limit
Reading supplied codeSOURCE, behaviour inferred from source
Calling a pure decisionPURE_FUNCTION, browser enforcement unverified
Middleware with substitute request/responseCALLBACK_MODEL, actual Express order unverified
Actual qualified application or browser runACTUAL_EXPRESS or REAL_BROWSER, with genuine locator
task: Keep the result and its evidence limit together

title: CORS and CSRF
body_html: The reduced portfolio records two defensive classes. Sharing a response across origins and protecting a cookie-authenticated write require different controls.
task: Trace both decisions in the supplied reduced route

title: Required reduced portfolio
body_html:
• CORS: exact-origin allowed/refused controls, sharing headers, credentials and Vary.
  • CSRF: safe methods and cookie-authenticated unsafe methods with match, missing and mismatch controls.

Two-class evidence leaves the other security classes unqualified.
task: Plan the required P03 work in the same S11 PDF

title: P01 capstone transfer
body_html:
Trace how the moderation policy will use authentication and session evidence in the semester project.

P01 integration occurs when separately scheduled. Advanced 11.3B remains optional.
task: Record the transfer plan without adding a hidden S11 requirement

title: Evidence draft and exit ticket
body_html:
Complete the next truthful checkpoint in the evidence form. Retain JSON as a portable draft backup.

Exit ticket: which control changed your prediction, and which evidence would strengthen your conclusion?
task: Record required work still outstanding and redact the draft

title: The complete 60-minute STOP
body_html:
At minute 60, STOP and retain the evidence draft.

Complete required P02, the reduced CORS/CSRF portfolio and the real bounded critique before the actual teacher-set deadline.

The completed route submits one reviewed PDF: TW2026_S11_GROUP_ALIAS.pdf. PDF review and the real Moodle submission remain separate actions.
task: Save the draft and name the next required evidence
